newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close flat, eye CA sale decision.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close flat, eye CA sale decision.

text.p: Austrian shares closed practically unchanged on Wednesday and traders said buyers were likely to remain elusive until a decision was made on the the sale of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips edged up 0.19 points or 0.02 percent to 1,137.28. Among its constituents 11 ATX shares rose and 10 fell.
Traders saw the index trading in a 1,130-to-1,140-point range for the time being.
"As long as the issue of Creditanstalt remains unresolved, we will continue to drift sideways," said one trader.

But he noted the index was well supported at 1,130. "The upward trend is not in danger," he said, adding the current stagnation of the market was psychologically motivated. "From the technical charts it doesn't look bad at all," he said.

Buying was mainly selective and in cyclical stocks, traders said. Stocks affected by the long-running Creditanstalt saga, namely insurer EA-Generali, Bank Austria and Creditanstalt, were the most volatile.
"They are playing out every rumour," said one trader.
Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said on Wednesday a decision on the sale of the flagship bank to one of three bidders must follow a January 10 deadline swiftly.

He rejected a compromise solution offered by government coalition partner the People's Party according to which half the state's stake in Creditanstalt should be sold to Bank Austria and the rest floated on the stock exchange.
Preferred shares of Bank Austria were the leading decliner, easing 1.65 percent to 398.3 schillings.
EA-Generali lost 1.27 percent at 3,100 schillings and Creditanstalt preferred shares were down 1.36 percent at 1,380 schillings.
The top gainer of the session was Austrian microchip maker AMS, climbing 3.52 percent to 876 schillings.
The January ATX future added 1.5 points to 1,136.5.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index shed 0.05 points or 0.01 percent to 427.63. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
